note: FAILED-path spec. Only the session evidence is required, because an early failure legitimately produces nothing else: a session that stopped in stage A has no journal, no telemetry and no selection, and demanding them would block the collection of what a failed run DOES have. Everything the search may have produced before it stopped is best-effort and collected if present -- a beam that ran for hours and then failed at commit has a journal and a telemetry stream worth keeping, and those are exactly the observations the next session's cost table pools over. Gated on presence, never on session success: `$2.82` of verified checkpoints were once lost to a collector keyed on `terminal == ALL_DONE`. On lifecycle: the vocabulary is `final_required` and `mutable_snapshot` and nothing else -- an invented word makes this document UNLOADABLE and the collector exits 1 before it looks at a single file.
